examples.text: Вдруг за этой дверью тоже что-то интересное.
examples.trans: What if there is something interesting behind this door too.

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'крыть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to open', paired with 'открывать'.

examples.text: Слушай, Эля, а ты не хочешь дверь открыть?

examples.text: Дима, немедленно открывай, я знаю, что ты здесь!
examples.trans: Dima, open up immediately, I know that you are in here!

examples.text: Откройте дверь.
examples.trans: Open the door.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'suddenly, what if', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: And in four years he has not had a single scratch.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'something; somehow', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Что-то Нагиев сегодня расщедрился, не находишь?
examples.trans: Nagiyev got awfully generous today, don't you find?

examples.trans: Has something happened?

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'нять'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'understood', paired with 'понимать'.

examples.text: Не поняла, о чём ты сейчас говоришь.
examples.trans: I do not understand what you are talking about right now.

examples.text: Всё понятно, спасибо за поздравление и прощай!
examples.trans: Everything is clear, thanks for the birthday wishes and goodbye!

examples.text: Ты же мужчина, ты должен меня понять!
examples.trans: You are a man, you must understand me!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'speak', paired with 'сказать'.

examples.text: Дима, ты мне это третий раз говоришь.
examples.trans: Dima, you are telling me that for the third time.

examples.text: Настя, что ты говоришь, ты же вегетарианка!
examples.trans: Nastya, what are you saying, you are a vegetarian!

examples.text: Ну что, мужики, теперь спокойно поговорим?
examples.trans: Well then, men, shall we have a quiet talk now?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'we', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы скидываемся по тысяче рублей, как обычно.
examples.trans: We are chipping in a thousand rubles each, as usual.

examples.text: Лёва, ты самый щедрый из нас человек.
examples.trans: Lyova, you are the most generous person among us.

examples.text: Мы по дороге чуть сына дома не забыли.
examples.trans: On the way we almost forgot our son at home.

meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'вести'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will expose / bring out'.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и вывести вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and will expose on time.

examples.text: На нашей кухне все умеют вывести.
examples.trans: In our kitchen everyone knows how to will expose.

examples.text: Он просто вообще об этом не знал!
examples.trans: He simply did not know about it at all!
